mainTopic: Separating תרומה for someone else (consent and טובת הנאה), and teaching Torah to someone under a vow of benefit
overview: The amud opens with a question. When a person separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's produce, does he need the friend's consent? The גמרא tries to prove the answer from our משנה, which lets a man under a vow (מודר הנאה) separate his fellow's תרומות and מעשרות 'לדעתו'. That proof is pushed away with רבא's case of an owner who says anyone may come and separate תרומה. Next, רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא who holds the טובת הנאה, meaning the right to choose the כהן: the one who gives the produce, or the owner of the pile? רבי זירא answers from a פסוק that it is the owner of the pile. רבי ירמיה challenges this from the משנה, and the same open-invitation case answers him. Then a ruling of רבי יוחנן says the separator holds the טובת הנאה, and the גמרא gives no reply. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that one may teach the man under the vow מדרש but not מקרא. שמואל explains it as a place where only מקרא teachers are paid, and the גמרא asks why the משנה then states it as a flat rule.

steps.title: Does tithing for someone else need his consent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a person who separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's produce needs the friend's consent. It gives two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's produce, does he need his friend's consent or not? Do we say that since it is a benefit for the friend, no consent is needed? Or maybe it is the friend's own מצוה, and he would rather do it himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Can you do another person's תרומה for him using your own produce, without asking him first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: you may do a favor for a person without his knowledge, and getting his produce fixed is a favor. Side two: the מצוה belongs to the owner, and he may want to do it himself, so it is not clearly a favor.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
It is pleasing to him / he prefers

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether doing a מצוה-related act for someone counts as a favor you may do without asking him.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
One who separates teruma from his own produce for that of his friend,
does he need his (the friend's) consent or not?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דִּזְכוּת הוּא לוֹ,
phrases.english: Do we say: since it is a benefit for him,
it does not need consent.
Or perhaps it is his own מצוה,
and he prefers to do it himself.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether separating תרומה from one's own produce for another's produce requires the owner's consent.

steps.title: Bringing the משנה as a possible proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. It says that someone under a vow may separate his fellow's תרומות and מעשרות 'with his knowledge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: he may separate his תרומות and his מעשרות with his knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from our משנה to try to answer the question. This is only the setup; the next steps will work out what the line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about two people with a vow between them, so one may not give the other any benefit. Even so, the משנה lets him separate the other's תרומות and מעשרות 'לדעתו', meaning 'with his knowledge.' The גמרא will now ask whose produce is used and whose knowledge is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: His תרומות (portions given to the כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לדעתו' is unclear on purpose. It could mean the owner's knowledge or the tither's own say-so. That is exactly what the גמרא is about to ask.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרֵם אֶת תְּרוּמוֹתָיו וְאֶת מַעְשְׂרוֹתָיו לְדַעְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: He separates his terumot and his tithes with his knowledge.
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה about a man who is forbidden by vow to give his fellow benefit. 'His' means the fellow's produce.

steps.raayaObject: The question of whether consent is needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: תורם את תרומותיו ואת מעשרותיו לדעתו

steps.title: Owner's produce on the tither's own say-so: who made him a שליח?
steps.stepSummary: The first reading is that he uses the owner's own produce, on his own say-so. This fails, because nobody appointed him as an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say he takes from the owner's pile for the owner's pile, then whose knowledge is meant? If his own knowledge, who appointed him as a שליח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing each way to read the משנה. First it tries this: he takes from the owner's pile, on his own say-so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot separate תרומה from another person's produce unless he made you his שליח. So this reading cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
Owner of the pile of grain

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא מִן בַּעַל הַכְּרִי עַל שֶׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי,
phrases.english: If you say from the pile-owner's produce for that of the pile-owner,
then with whose knowledge?
If you say with his own (the tither's) knowledge —
who made him an agent?

steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as: owner's produce, tither's own say-so
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separating from someone else's produce needs שליחות, and here no one appointed him.

steps.title: Owner's produce with the owner's consent: that is a benefit
steps.stepSummary: The next reading is the owner's produce with the owner's consent. This fails, because acting as the owner's שליח is a benefit, and the vow forbids that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means with the owner's knowledge. But then he is giving him a benefit, since he is acting as his שליח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the next reading: the owner asked him to do it. It rejects this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner appointed him, then he is doing a job for the owner. That is a real benefit, and the vow forbids giving one. So the משנה could not allow it.

phrases.english: Rather, with the knowledge of the pile-owner.
But he is benefiting him,
since he is doing his errand as his agent!

steps.kashyaTarget: Reading: owner's produce with the owner's consent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doing someone's שליחות is a benefit, and the vow forbids giving him benefit.

steps.title: Tither's own produce with the owner's consent: still a benefit
steps.stepSummary: The next reading is that he uses his own produce, but with the owner's consent. This also fails, because it is still a benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he uses his own produce for the pile. With whose knowledge? If with the owner's knowledge, he is giving him a benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to a case where the tither uses his own produce. First it tests the option that the owner agreed, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with his own produce, if he does it because the owner asked, he is again doing the owner's errand. That is again a forbidden benefit.

phrases.english: Rather, from his own produce for that of the pile.
And with whose knowledge?
If you say with the knowledge of the pile-owner —
but he is benefiting him!

steps.kashyaTarget: Reading: tither's own produce with the owner's consent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acting at the owner's request is still שליחות, so it is still a benefit.

steps.title: Only one reading is left: no consent is needed
steps.stepSummary: The only reading left is his own produce on his own say-so. That shows a person may do another's תרומה from his own produce without the owner's consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it that he acts on his own say-so, using his own produce for his friend's? And if you say consent is needed, that would make it a benefit! So isn't it that no consent is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the one reading that still works and draws the proof from it. No consent is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If consent were needed, this case would also be agency and so a forbidden benefit, and the משנה would not allow it. Since the משנה does allow it, doing it from your own produce must work without the owner's consent. This would answer the question from Step 1, but the next step rejects the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that… (drawing a conclusion)
And if you were to say

phrases.english: Rather, is it not with his own knowledge,
and he separates from his own for his friend's?
And if you say it needs consent —
then he would be benefiting him!
Rather, is it not that it does not need consent?

steps.raayaObject: That separating from one's own produce for another does not need the owner's consent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The process of elimination on the משנה's words 'לדעתו'

steps.title: Rejecting the proof with רבא's case of an open invitation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. The משנה can be talking about the owner's own produce, where the owner announced that anyone may come and separate תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is from the owner's pile for the owner's pile. As רבא said: it is where the owner says 'Anyone who wants to separate תרומה may come and do it.' Here too, it is where he says that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It goes back to the first reading (the owner's own produce) and explains how that reading can work after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 failed because nobody made him a שליח. But if the owner gave an open invitation to anyone, then he is allowed to separate, and he is not doing a personal errand for the owner. So it is not a forbidden benefit. Because of this, the משנה proves nothing about our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Anyone who wants to separate תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה is rejected. The משנה can mean the owner's own produce with an open invitation to anyone, which is neither appointing a שליח nor a personal favor. So the question of whether consent is needed is still open.
steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say consent is needed. It only shows that the משנה does not prove either side.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי עַל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי,
phrases.english: Actually, it is from the pile-owner's produce for the pile-owner's,
as Rava said:
where he says, 'Anyone who wishes to separate teruma may come and separate,'
here too, it is where he says, etc.
phrases.notes: 'וכו׳' means the same announcement as before: anyone who wants may come and separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי עַל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The process of elimination missed a case: the owner's own produce with a general invitation. That case needs no specific שליחות and gives no personal benefit.

steps.title: Who gets to choose the כהן when separating for someone else?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the טובת הנאה belongs to the one who gives the produce or to the owner of the pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: If someone separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's pile, who has the right to choose the כהן? Do we say the separator does, because without his produce the friend's pile would never be fixed? Or do we say the owner does, because without the owner's pile the separator's produce would never become תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. When one person's produce is used as תרומה for another person's pile, who decides which כהן receives it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side needs the other. The separator supplies the actual produce, and the owner's pile is what makes that produce count as תרומה. The question is which of these two contributions makes someone the 'giver' who controls the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces a real question between scholars)
The right to choose which כהן gets the gift (worth something, since a friend may pay for it)
Becomes fixed, made permitted to eat after תרומה is taken

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether helping someone by separating his תרומה gives him something of value, which matters for the vow case in our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
One who separates teruma from his own produce for his friend's produce,
whose is the right to choose the priest?
Do we say:
if not for the produce of this one (the separator),
phrases.notes: Read this as a question: could the pile get fixed without his produce? No. So he should be the one who chooses.

phrases.english: would that one's pile be fixed?
Or perhaps:
if not for that one's pile (the owner's),
this one's produce would not become teruma?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that grows out of the earlier discussion of separating תרומה for someone else.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When תרומה is separated from A's produce for B's pile, does A or B hold the טובת הנאה?

steps.title: רבי זירא answers from a פסוק: the owner of the pile chooses
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא cites a פסוק showing that the giving belongs to the person whose produce is being fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: The פסוק says, 'All the produce of your seed... and you shall give.' This shows that the one whose produce it is does the giving.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that the טובת הנאה belongs to the owner of the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the giving to 'your' produce, meaning the produce that needs fixing. So the person whose pile is being fixed counts as the giver and decides which כהן gets the gift.

phrases.english: He said to him: the verse says:
"All the produce of your seed... and you shall give."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טובת הנאה belongs to the owner of the pile, based on 'your produce... and you shall give'.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה challenges from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: If the owner holds the טובת הנאה, separating for him gives him a benefit, so the person under the vow should not be allowed to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: Our משנה says the person under the vow may separate the other man's תרומות and מעשרות with his knowledge. But if the טובת הנאה belongs to the owner of the pile, the separator is giving him a benefit! So learn from this that the טובת הנאה belongs to the separator.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's answer using the משנה about the man who is forbidden by vow to give his friend any benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the person under the vow separate תרומה for his friend. If that left the owner holding a valuable right, it would be a benefit, and the vow forbids benefits. So the משנה seems to show the separator keeps the טובת הנאה, which goes against רבי זירא.

phrases.english: He challenged him:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרֵם אֶת תְּרוּמוֹתָיו וְאֶת מַעְשְׂרוֹתָיו לְדַעְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: He may separate his teruma and his tithes with his knowledge.
And if you say
the right to choose belongs to the owner of the pile,
then he is benefiting him!
Rather, learn from it
that the right to choose is his (the separator's).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 9, using the reading of the משנה from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's ruling that the owner of the pile holds the טובת הנאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows the man under the vow to separate for his friend. If that gave the owner the טובת הנאה, it would be a forbidden benefit. So the separator must be the one who holds it.

steps.title: The case is the owner's own produce, open to anyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the challenge away. The משנה is talking about the owner's produce, where the owner invited anyone to separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: No. The משנה means he separates from the owner's produce for the owner's pile, with the owner's consent, where the owner said, 'Anyone who wants to separate תרומה may come and separate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge by reusing the explanation it already gave in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the produce is the owner's and the owner told everyone they may separate, the man under the vow is not doing him a special favor or acting as his personal agent. So the משנה proves nothing about whose טובת הנאה it is, and רבי זירא's answer still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Anyone who wants to separate תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new idea. It is the same answer as step 7, now used to defend רבי זירא against the new challenge.

phrases.english: They say: No,

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי עַל שֶׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי,
phrases.english: it is from the owner of the pile's produce for the owner of the pile's produce,
and with the knowledge of the owner of the pile,
where he says:
"Anyone who wants to separate teruma may come and separate."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לֹא, מִשֶּׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי עַל שֶׁל בַּעַל הַכְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by reusing the case explanation from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The challenge's reading of the משנה as the separator using his own produce
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be talking about the owner's own produce with an open invitation to anyone, so no personal benefit is given and nothing is proven about the טובת הנאה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the separator holds the טובת הנאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that one who separates from his own produce for someone else holds the טובת הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When one person consecrates an animal for another's atonement, the one who consecrated it adds the fifth when redeeming it, and the one being atoned for is the one who can make a תמורה. And one who separates תרומה from his own produce for produce that is not his holds the טובת הנאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to settle רבי ירמיה's question, and it seems to go against רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן splits the rights between the two people in the case of a קרבן, and he rules directly that the separator who uses his own produce holds the טובת הנאה. This is the opposite of what רבי זירא said in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who consecrates the animal
Adds a fifth when redeeming something holy
The one the קרבן brings atonement for
Swapping a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct ruling against רבי זירא's answer. The גמרא brings no reply and moves on to the next line of the משנה, so רבי יוחנן's ruling stands as the answer to רבי ירמיה's question: the separator holds the טובת הנאה.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Abahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The one who consecrates adds the fifth,
phrases.notes: The case is one person setting aside an animal as a קרבן for someone else's atonement.

phrases.english: and the one being atoned for makes a substitute.
And one who separates teruma from his own produce for what is not his —
the right to choose is his.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to settle the question of step 8, against the answer of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the separator, not the owner of the pile, holds the טובת הנאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'one who separates from his own for what is not his, the טובת הנאה is his'

steps.title: The משנה allows teaching מדרש but not מקרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a person may teach the one under the vow מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, but not מקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may teach him מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, but he may not teach him מקרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who is forbidden by a נדר to get any benefit from someone else. The משנה lets that someone teach him the oral parts of Torah, but not the written Torah. The difference between the two is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning laws by explaining the words of the פסוקים
Fixed laws of the oral Torah
Non-legal teachings and stories of the oral Torah
The written Torah, the text of תנ"ך

phrases.english: He may teach him midrash, halakhot and aggadot,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the person who is forbidden by vow to get any benefit from the teacher.

phrases.english: but he may not teach him Bible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of separating תרומה to a new line in the משנה about teaching Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching מדרש, הלכות and אגדות is allowed to someone under the vow; teaching מקרא is not.

steps.title: Teaching מדרש is also a benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if מקרא is forbidden because teaching gives benefit, then teaching מדרש gives benefit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why may he not teach him מקרא? Because it benefits him? Teaching מדרש also benefits him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's split between מקרא and מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason to forbid teaching מקרא would be that the student gets a benefit from the teacher. But learning מדרש is just as much a benefit. So the line the משנה draws seems to make no sense.

phrases.english: Bible, what is the reason he may not teach him?
Because he is giving him benefit?
With midrash he is also giving him benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מקרא is forbidden but מדרש is allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both kinds of teaching give the student benefit, so the reason for forbidding מקרא should forbid מדרש too.

steps.title: שמואל: a place where only מקרא teachers are paid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about a place where people pay for learning מקרא but not for learning מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: this is in a place where people take pay for teaching מקרא, but do not take pay for teaching מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by setting the משנה in a specific kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that place, teaching מקרא for free saves the student money he would normally pay, and that savings is a forbidden benefit. Teaching מדרש is free everywhere there, so the student saves nothing. The difference is about money, not about the kind of Torah.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
In a place where they take payment for teaching Bible
and they do not take payment for teaching midrash.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹטְלִין שָׂכָר עַל הַמִּקְרָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה to a specific local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to forbid מקרא simply because teaching is a benefit, which would also forbid מדרש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden benefit is the saved tuition, which exists only for מקרא in a place where it is paid for.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the real benefit in question is money saved, not the learning itself.

steps.title: Why does the משנה state the rule without qualification?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the משנה states its rule as if it is true everywhere, not only in certain places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it stated as a fixed rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything depends on local custom, the משנה should not have stated flatly that מקרא is forbidden and מדרש is allowed. The plain wording sounds like a rule for every place, and there is no built-in difference between מקרא and מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it stated as a flat rule, with no conditions?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not asking what שמואל meant. It is asking why the משנה would word a local-custom rule as if it applied everywhere.

phrases.english: Why is it stated without qualification?
phrases.notes: Literally "what cut it off?" It means: why did the משנה make it a flat rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 15 by pointing to the flat wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's limiting of the משנה to a place where only מקרא teachers are paid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה draws a fixed line between מקרא and מדרש, which does not fit a rule that depends on local custom.
